origin: Own exact nondispersive, nonmagnetic, lossless two-dielectric mathematical model. Neither calibrated refractive indices nor finite-stack outputs are empirical measurements of the cited experiment. Frequencies and lengths are normalized to a known vacuum reference wavelength lambda0. The fixed source is a noiseless bulk-curvature oracle, not a truncated finite-frequency measurement.
calibration: Two homogeneous layers form a period, ordered1 then2. Their unknown positive indices satisfy n2>n1>1.4. Their independently known optical thicknesses are n1*d1/lambda0=n2*d2/lambda0=1/4. Let f=vacuum_frequency/reference_frequency and q=k_parallel/(2*pi*f/lambda0). For TE bulk half-trace B_TE(f,q), the exact Taylor coefficient is B_TE=1-(pi^2/8)h(q)f^2+O(f^4). The CSV supplies three exact h values as rational strings at rational q, in shuffled order. Infer the indices using ALL rows, actual LinearLeastSquares for the complete h versus q^2 fit, and actual PolynomialRoots for the complete ratio polynomial before applying index ordering. Derive why normal-incidence BULK dispersion alone leaves an absolute-index scale gauge even with both optical thicknesses known. This does not assert invariance of finite air-interface reflectance. Retain complete physical branch and domain reasoning when angular data remove the gauge.
bulk_definition: For a layer j with propagating phase c_j(q)=sqrt(1-q^2/n_j^2), delta_j=(pi*f/2)c_j, define Y_j_TE=n_j*c_j and Y_j_TM=n_j/c_j. The real transfer convention is M_j=[[cos(delta_j),sin(delta_j)/Y_j],[-Y_j*sin(delta_j),cos(delta_j)]]. A period is M2*M1, determinant1. Bloch multipliers are eigenvalues of this complete period matrix. Its half-trace B has a stopband exactly where |B|>1. The first stopband is the possible connected interval bounded by the FIRST two positive antiperiodic edges B=-1; do not confuse a finite slab interference minimum with an infinite-periodic bulk edge.
continuous_gap_certificate: Find both first-gap edges at q=0 and at q=1 for TE and TM, including possible gap closure. Determine the common FIRST bulk stopband for BOTH polarizations and EVERY q in the CLOSED interval[0,1], explicitly including the q=1 grazing-limit bulk problem in this criterion. Report its lower/upper boundary and whether endpoints belong. Derive the completeness/uniqueness of the first two positive edges rather than root-search one guessed branch. Establish a continuous-angle certificate for the extrema that control this intersection; a finite angular or frequency grid is not sufficient. You may derive the antiperiodic scalar Maxwell variational problems, with interface continuity and Bloch antiperiodic boundary conditions, or give another complete argument. The closed-q bulk criterion is deliberately distinguished from power transport at exactly grazing external incidence.
Brewster_test: Keep the inferred fixed layered material but enlarge the closed tangential-index interval to[0,1.4]; every layer still propagates. Determine the positive TM admittance-matching q_B, and whether ANY positive-frequency interval, in ANY band, can be a common bulk stopband for both polarizations throughout this enlarged q range. An isolated matching q can defeat a claimed common gap; do not infer the result from the original air light-cone range or only from normal incidence.
finite_stack_audit: At f=1,q=0.8, separately for TE and TM, retain actual MatrixMultiply of M2*M1, actual successive full-matrix products M^2,M^4,M^8, and actual PolynomialRoots of the full Bloch characteristic polynomial. Use the actual returned matrices and complete root inventory, selecting the decaying multiplier and its phase. Both ambient half-spaces have n0=1, with Y0_TE=sqrt(1-q^2) and Y0_TM=1/sqrt(1-q^2). For this real-transfer convention the eight-period power transmittance is T8=4/[(M8_11+M8_22)^2+(Y0*M8_12-M8_21/Y0)^2]. Derive or verify the matching/power balance, report T8,R8,absorbed fraction, and compare exact T8 with exp(-16*kappa), where kappa=-log|lambda_decay| is AMPLITUDE attenuation per period. Report decaying Bloch phase in[0,2*pi). Distinguish reflection, amplitude decay, power transmission and material absorption; absence of propagating bulk Bloch modes does not create dissipation in a lossless medium. Do not replace actual finite matrix propagation with the bare exponential factor.

interpretation_proposals.A: Angularly resolved bulk curvature can break an absolute-index scale gauge present in normal-incidence bulk dispersion.
interpretation_proposals.B: A grid of angles and frequencies that contains no propagating point proves a continuous omnidirectional gap.
interpretation_proposals.C: A TM admittance-matching tangential index can close every TM bulk stopband, defeating a common-gap claim over a range containing it.
interpretation_proposals.D: A negative real decaying Bloch multiplier has zero phase advance per period.
interpretation_proposals.E: Bulk evanescence and near-unit reflectance are compatible with zero material absorption.
interpretation_proposals.F: The Bloch attenuation exponent alone fixes the exact transmission of any finite slab independently of boundary admittances.
interpretation_proposals.G: An omnidirectional common gap at the original external-index range must persist when that range is enlarged.
interpretation_proposals.H: An exact continuous-domain band-edge argument must separate bulk grazing-limit conditions from finite power transport at grazing incidence.

reporting: Use the public answer schema, numeric tolerance1e-7absolute; complete ratio roots ascending, layer quantities layer1then2, every edgepair increasing. All gap boundaries are frequencies normalized to the reference frequency. Finite Bloch multipliers are real and ordered decaying first then growing; attenuation is nonnegative amplitude exponent per period. Strict gap and index-domain membership, endpoint inclusion and losslessness remain exact logical requirements even near a boundary. Supply identification, complete edge and continuous-angle arguments in the trajectory; answer fields report compact numerical conclusions.
